explanation: Keep two pointers k nodes apart, starting from a dummy predecessor. When the leading pointer reaches the tail, the trailing pointer precedes the kth-last node. Bypass that node; the dummy handles deleting the head.
timeComplexity: O(n) Both pointers move forward at most n links.
spaceComplexity: O(1) Only a dummy predecessor and two pointers are needed.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: After advancing fast by k links, the pointers stay k nodes apart. When fast reaches the tail, slow is exactly the predecessor of the kth-last node. Bypassing that successor deletes the requested position; a dummy predecessor makes head deletion identical.
walkthrough: For [7,5,9,2] and k=4, the kth-last node is the head 7. The dummy predecessor bypasses it, returning [5,9,2].
edgeCases: k equal to list length removes the head.
The contract supplies a valid positive k.
